## Classification and scope
Reproduced by the repository's hosted CI on **unmerged PR #24**, exact head `f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82`. This is not a claim about a published package or deployed service. Independent review inspected the logs and exact source; it did not rerun the complete suite locally.

Canonical owner: [pm-swarm-y972](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/.agents/pm/features/pm-swarm-y972.toon). Its full-quality-gate and privacy-admission acceptance must preserve ordinary fenced lifecycle workflows.

## Evidence / reproduction
Both [Node 26 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40402171049/job/121850578644) and [Node 22.18.0 job](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/actions/runs/40402171049/job/121850578403) finish the suite with **382 tests, 378 pass, 4 fail**. The four existing scenarios fail when closing received/reclaimed work:

- [fair-scheduling.test.ts:92–99](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/test/fair-scheduling.test.ts#L92-L99): explicit handoff to a qualified receiver, then `receiver.close`.
- [fencing.test.ts:22–47](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/test/fencing.test.ts#L22-L47): round-trip fenced handoff, then valid close.
- [fencing.test.ts:53–77](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/test/fencing.test.ts#L53-L77): reclaimed legacy claim assigned to receiver, then close.
- [fencing.test.ts:117–130](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/test/fencing.test.ts#L117-L130): native registered-command sequence; close returns exit **2**, expected **0**.

Actual error: `swarm_document_changed`, with remedy “The item changed after admission; refresh its complete document, re-evaluate ownership and retry with the current receipt.”

The stack reaches [SharedTracker.close](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/src/shared-tracker.ts#L327-L335) through the new [locked document comparison](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/f44ed39833a6b858a3aa2ea2e6503a53e948fc82/src/settings.ts#L53-L88). These sequential fixtures do not intentionally introduce a competing document write at close. The exact mismatch/root cause has **not** been isolated; do not assume disabling comparison or retrying all refusals is a valid fix.

To reproduce, use the existing repository release/coverage gate on this immutable head and pinned SDK `2026.10.23`, or its named fencing/fair-scheduling scenarios in an isolated fixture. Hosted full-gate commands and logs are linked above. Coverage also falls below unchanged 100% thresholds (99.96% statements/lines, 99.84% branches), but the functional refusals are the primary finding.

## Expected / impact
A current owner with a valid fence should close completed handoff/reclaimed work, receive the success receipt, persist closed status, remove ownership/handoff fields and advance the generation. The current PR instead refuses these supported workflows, blocking full release admission and potentially leaving otherwise-completed tasks open if merged.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
- Identify and fix the actual snapshot/native-hook mismatch without removing whole-document/privacy admission, stale-revision protection or fence checks.
- All four existing scenarios pass on supported Node 22.18.0 and 26; native CLI close exits 0 and preserves expected item/history/receipt outcomes.
- Keep negative controls for stale peers, ABA fences, altered bodies and private values failing before persistence.
- Full npm/Bun gates and unchanged coverage thresholds pass on the final head; record publication separately from merge.

All-status repository issues/PRs and current PR discussion/canonical feature were checked before filing; no separate matching regression issue was present. This evidence supplements the existing PR/feature owner, not a competing implementation.

The previous valid-close-after-handoff/reclaim failures do not recur on this head.

The [native commit observer](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/a4dc37cff9f1e631a7bdd9e17082aa5a0417eefb/src/settings.ts) advances the admitted snapshot only for its exact committed before/after successor; later failure reports `swarm_partial_commit` instead of suggesting nothing committed. > - An independent bounded Node 24.22.1 check of the exact extracted guard/fingerprint/observer logic passed **11 assertions** for successor admission, unrelated notification rejection, peer mismatch and pre-/post-commit interruptions. That check uses synthetic hook contexts and a stub privacy classifier/SDK identity: it is **not** an independent full native-SDK or package-suite rerun.
> 
> The remaining atomicity limitation is explicitly tracked in the actual [`pm-swarm-atomic-close` record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/a4dc37cff9f1e631a7bdd9e17082aa5a0417eefb/.agents/pm/issues/pm-swarm-atomic-close.toon) and [privacy-admission documentation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/blob/a4dc37cff9f1e631a7bdd9e17082aa5a0417eefb/docs/privacy-admission.md): pinned SDK compound update/close remains two native commits. Per-stage guards and truthful partial receipts do not establish single-commit or crash-all-or-nothing semantics. Preserve that follow-up and the negative controls; verify the final merged/published artifact separately.
